documents.title: Chat GPT & AI Support (sample syllabus statements)
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule of its own: 'Faculty may wish to allow students to use generative AI tools, provide specific parameters for its use, or prohibit its use', and offers three sample statements (no use, some use, full use), so the decision is left to faculty and the page is a set of tiers.
documents.summary: An ITLE teaching-center page of 2023 that explains ChatGPT and its limits and tells faculty to state their AI position in the syllabus and Canvas. It offers three OSU sample statements (prohibit, limited, full use with attribution) plus statements from other universities, and ends with ways to make assignments harder to complete with AI.

documents.stance_why: The page governs how instructors respond to 'students have violated academic integrity policies by misusing AI' and leaves what counts as misuse to the instructor's own policy ('update assignment guidelines'); it sets no AI use rule, so it delegates.
documents.summary: ITLE guidance of November 2025 for instructors who suspect AI misuse. notes: Coded by Coder A. Statements quoted from other institutions (Texas Tech, Iowa, Colorado, Minnesota, UMass Amherst) on the ITLE sample-syllabus page are coded as units because the page offers them to faculty as templates; the OSU samples are the university's own. No school or computing documents were collected; the course layer was deferred.
